title: Fine-Tuned LLMs are “Time Capsules” for Tracking Societal Bias Through Books
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the association of religious groups with specific positive and negative societal roles and activities (e.g., defacing a monument, credit card fraud, providing free literacy, holiday decorations) to track temporal shifts in societal biases as reflected in literature.
findings: Fine-tuned LLMs reflect historical societal biases from the books they were trained on. Specifically, the association of Islam with negative activities (like 'defacing a monument') rose sharply from 22% in the 1950s to 48% in the 2010s, with a significant increase in the 2000s, which likely reflects post-9/11 societal attitudes.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models.
